    Homogeneous components of composites in kQ #

    Composition with a homogeneous morphism of degree m shifts homogeneous components by m. Together with the finiteness of the decomposition into components, this reduces statements about the mesh sequences of C(Q, c) to homogeneous families (graded-category.tex).

    source
    theorem MultiplicativeBasisDeformations.LinearPaths.proj_comp_of_mem {k : Type u} [Field k] {V : Type v} [Quiver V] {m d : ℕ} {x y z : V} (F : obj x ⟶ obj y) {G : obj y ⟶ obj z} (hG : G ∈ degreePart m y z) :
    (proj (d + m) x z) (CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp F G) = CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp ((proj d x y) F) G

    (proj e x z) (CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp F G) = 0
    source
    theorem MultiplicativeBasisDeformations.LinearPaths.proj_of_mem_comp {k : Type u} [Field k] {V : Type v} [Quiver V] {m d : ℕ} {x y z : V} {G : obj x ⟶ obj y} (hG : G ∈ degreePart m x y) (F : obj y ⟶ obj z) :
    (proj (m + d) x z) (CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp G F) = CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp G ((proj d y z) F)

    (proj e x z) (CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp G F) = 0

    theorem MultiplicativeBasisDeformations.LinearPaths.eq_sum_proj_of_le {k : Type u} [Field k] {V : Type v} [Quiver V] {x y : V} (f : obj x ⟶ obj y) :
    ∃ (N : ℕ), ∀ (M : ℕ), N ≤ M → f = ∑ d ∈ Finset.range M, (proj d x y) f

    The decomposition into homogeneous components may use any long enough range of degrees.

    theorem MultiplicativeBasisDeformations.LinearPaths.exists_sum_proj_family {k : Type u} [Field k] {V : Type v} [Quiver V] {α : Type u_1} [Fintype α] {x y : α → V} (f : (a : α) → obj (x a) ⟶ obj (y a)) :
    ∃ (N : ℕ), ∀ (a : α), f a = ∑ d ∈ Finset.range N, (proj d (x a) (y a)) (f a)

    A uniform range of degrees for a finite family.
